gpt.text:
Given this handoff, you’re in a clean state: there’s a current champion (`baseline/champion_v5_latest.json`), no PASS candidates, and nothing marked inconclusive. The “Next Commands” are the right sequence to (1) explore module variants, (2) explore system-level candidates, and (3) generate a targeted fix plan.

Run them in the order listed:

```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --run --select-best
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml --run
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```

### What each step will do / what to look for

1) **`aub_autopilot.py ... --select-best` (module-level sweep + selection)**
- Runs candidate module variations from `module_registry.yaml`.
- Compares against the current champion and promotes the best if it meets the PASS criteria.
- After it finishes, check:
  - whether a new “PASS candidate” was created/promoted
  - updated metrics (especially the same two you’re tracking: `tuning_*` and `lockbox_*`)
  - any failure modes (timeouts, flaky tests, regressions)

2) **`system_autopilot.py ...` (system-level candidate sweep)**
- Tries end-to-end/system configuration candidates from `system_candidates.yaml`.
- Useful if module-level tweaks aren’t moving metrics or if interactions matter.
- After it finishes, look for:
  - any system candidate beating the champion on your selection rule
  - any new “INCONCLUSIVE” entries (often indicates variance/flakiness)

3) **`aub_next_fix.py ...` (generate an actionable fix plan)**
- Produces `baseline/reports/next_fix.md` with the recommended next changes based on what just happened (wins, losses, failure patterns).
- This is the artifact you’d hand to someone to implement the next targeted adjustment.

### If you paste results, I can help decide quickly
After running, paste (or attach) the console summaries and any generated report snippets (especially the final comparison table and any “selected best” output). I can then:
- confirm whether the champion should be updated,
- diagnose why no PASS candidates emerged (if that happens),
- suggest adjustments to the candidate specs/registry to reduce variance or target the bottleneck implied by the tuning vs lockbox gap.
